6. In 1988, during the second mission after the Challenger disaster, a piece of insulation struck X’s underside just 85 seconds after liftoff. It severely damaged over 700 tiles and completely knocked one off. When the crew sent images of the damage to Mission Control, the encrypted satellite link was so poor that engineers dismissed the gashes as "lights and shadows."  Upon landing, engineers were horrified to find a massive hole in the shuttle’s belly. X only survived because the missing tile happened to be located directly over a thick steel mounting plate for an antenna, which prevented the superheated plasma from burning through the aluminum hull. Commander "Hoot" Gibson later said he was certain they were going to die during reentry.  Id X
